[[File:Endor_Holocaust.jpg|thumb|250px|An illustration of a stormtrooper's account of what he believed happened to the Ewoks.]]
{{Quote|That's a myth. Everyone knows most of the Death Star simply vaporized, and the Rebel Fleet intercepted the rest of the wreckage.|A patron of [[Mad Anghus's Fun Public House]], to a [[Unidentified stormtrooper (Apocalypse Endor)|veteran stormtrooper]]|<ref name="AE">{{Tales|14|Apocalypse Endor}}</ref>}}
After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Propaganda/Legends|propaganda]] agents claiming that the destruction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] over [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] caused a '''disaster''' on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] and that caused its inhabitants to be devastated by falling debris.<ref name="Wedge's Gamble">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref> However, the moon and its primary [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]], the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], and its countless overlooked secondary sentient species, were both all still in good health long after the Death Star's destruction, and the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] established a base on the moon.<ref name="TAB">''[[The Truce at Bakura]]''</ref> Much of the debris of the [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] was sent through a [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Wormhole/Legends|wormhole]] that briefly opened up when the Death Star's [[Hyperdrive regulator/Legends|hyperdrive regulator]] was destroyed. This matter was scattered across the galaxy,<ref name="GODV">''[[The Glove of Darth Vader]]''</ref> while the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] put much effort into stopping the remaining debris from colliding with the moon.<ref name="X-Wing: Rogue Leader 1">[[X-Wing: Rogue Leader 1|''X-Wing: Rogue Leader'' 1]]</ref><ref name="Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>

A [[Unidentified stormtrooper (Apocalypse Endor)|veteran stormtrooper]] of the Battle of Endor spoke of the supposed destruction of the forest moon, telling many that billions of tons of metal rained down on the moon and wiped out the Ewoks. His claims were countered by others, though, who claimed that it was simply myth. According to the man's fellow [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] patrons, most of the Death Star's mass was obliterated in the explosion, while the Rebel Alliance used [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beams]] to ensure the rest did not damage the world.<ref name="AE" />

At least one Imperial [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] did crash onto the moon's surface, though,<ref name="M">{{Tales|22|Marooned}}</ref> and some debris was reported to have caused minor damage to Ewok habitats.<ref name="Fury">''[[Legacy of the Force: Fury]]''</ref><ref name="Gamer">{{GamerCite|9|Endor and the Moddell Sector}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Ds2destroyed.png|thumb|324x324px|The explosion could be seen from the moon's surface. Note that some debris can clearly be seen shooting out of the explosion towards the moon.]]
The theory that such a disaster occurred was first proposed by [[Curtis Saxton]] on his [[Curtis Saxton|''Star Wars Technical Commentaries'']] fan site. Saxton, who referred to the event as the "Endor Holocaust," claimed that the disaster is scientifically inevitable, although it has never been reported in any [[canon]] source. Some sources, such as ''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]'' and the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] "[[Apocalypse Endor]]," refer to the event as being either propaganda or myth.<ref name="Wedge's Gamble" />

In [[Star Wars Insider 76|''Star Wars Insider'' 76]], a question and answer column written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] states that the Ewoks were not all killed after the Battle of Endor. He refers to events described in the juvenile novel ''[[The Glove of Darth Vader]]'', where debris from the second Death Star's destruction, including [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Glove of Darth Vader|glove]], is sucked through a wormhole and taken through [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] to the other end of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] (and, therefore, avoids landing on the forest moon). Hidalgo also acknowledges the environmental consequences expected from the destruction of a planetoid-sized battle station so close to a habitable moon, but claims that the laws of physics can be "thrown out the window" for the sake of a story which [[George Lucas]] intended to have a "happy ending".<ref name="SWI 76">[[Star Wars Insider 76|''Star Wars Insider'' 76]]</ref>

The extended version of the ''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode II]]'' special features a skit which humorously depicts the event.<ref name="RC II">''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode II]]''</ref>

Several years after [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney's]] [[2012]] acquisition of [[Lucasfilm]], the official ''Star Wars'' [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] account made a post giving the [[canon]] explanation that the Rebels set up shields and tractor beams to protect the [[moon]] from debris from the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]].<ref name="Endor Debris">{{Twitter|starwars|status/790904500768866304|Star Wars|quote=The Rebel Alliance fleet deployed shields and tractor beams to prevent Death Star 2's meteroric debris from devastating Endor's forest moon.|archivefile=File:SWTweetEndorDebris.png}}</ref> The [[2019]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']] depicts that the remains of the second Death Star fell on the [[ocean]] moon of [[Kef Bir]], located in the [[Endor system]].<ref name="Episode IX">{{Film|IX}}</ref> The accompanying reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'', written by Hidalgo, furthermore specifies that the [[Moddell sector]] is rife with [[Hyperspace anomaly|hyperspace anomalies]] which dumped the [[Death Star]] debris on Kef Bir, catastrophically displacing the moon's wildlife with the pollution in the oceans where the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station's]] reactor sunk into.<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>
